Route 157, Glen Carbon, Illinois, in 3026

You stand on Route 157 at Chain of Rocks Road, at the foot of the bluff above the Mississippi's floodplain, on a hot July afternoon a thousand years from now. This is one best guess, not a prediction: what today's trends (population, climate, how long buildings and roads last, energy, farming) would most likely make of this place. Signs explain each guess: its reasons, and how unsure anyone could be. Look at one and press E.

The ground is real (USGS elevations). Today's roads, from OpenStreetMap, are drawn as faint lines where they used to run; G hides them. Most of today's subdivisions are old forest, with the foundations of the houses under the leaves; Route 157 is a narrow, shaded road for small automated pods; the university town and Glen Carbon's old village centre are towns of thick-walled, shaded buildings; the interstate's embankment carries an electric railway. Pod stops at the crossroads go to the university town and to Glen Carbon village.
